projects.title: Pinhole
projects.oneLiner: A centimetre-tall hunter clears rooms under an old house and banishes bosses.

hotspots.title: Light is the mechanic
hotspots.text: The hunter's lantern lights a small circle: everything outside it is a risk, which is the whole tension of the game.

hotspots.title: Hearts and ammo together
hotspots.text: Health and shots sit in one compact badge, so a glance tells you if you can take the next fight.

hotspots.title: Room map
hotspots.text: A tiny map of the floor shows cleared rooms, to keep a run oriented under an old house.

hotspots.title: Thumb-sized controls
hotspots.text: Joystick left, Dash right, both large and semi-transparent: made for playing on a phone held sideways.

projects.title: DDF
projects.oneLiner: Tavern card brawl: table on the big screen, your hand on your phone; bots too.

hotspots.title: Your hand stays private
hotspots.text: Cards live on your phone; the TV shows only their backs, so bluffing works in a living room.

hotspots.title: Faces on the table
hotspots.text: Every player and bot sits around one table with a health bar, so the TV reads like a board game.

hotspots.title: Whose turn
hotspots.text: A single line at the top says who moves now, readable from the sofa.

projects.title: Corder
projects.oneLiner: Local meeting recorder and transcriber for Mac, no bot in the call.

hotspots.title: Recording on the side
hotspots.text: The live call stays visible while you read the transcript, so you never lose context.

hotspots.title: Speakers named
hotspots.text: Each line is attributed to a speaker, which makes the transcript usable as meeting notes.

hotspots.title: Who talked how much
hotspots.text: A speaker timeline shows the balance of the conversation at a glance.

hotspots.title: Every meeting searchable
hotspots.text: All recordings are local and searchable from the sidebar.

projects.title: Cromwell Wilkes
projects.oneLiner: Redesign of a London barrister-led immigration law firm website.

hotspots.title: Trust in the headline
hotspots.text: 'Barrister-Led Law Firm in London' says who they are and why it matters in one line.

hotspots.title: Proof before the fold
hotspots.text: Accreditation, a 4.9 Google rating and a refund guarantee answer a client's first worries.

hotspots.title: Call or write
hotspots.text: Phone number and 'Get in touch' are always visible, because most clients want to talk first.

hotspots.title: Local photograph
hotspots.text: Hammersmith Bridge grounds the firm in London without stock photos of handshakes.

projects.title: Trypillia
projects.oneLiner: Grow a Trypillian community from a few families into a proto-city.

hotspots.title: A real settlement plan
hotspots.text: Houses form rings like real Trypillian proto-cities; the layout is the history lesson.

hotspots.title: Fields as resources
hotspots.text: Ploughed fields at the edge show where food comes from before any tooltip does.

hotspots.title: Big, warm scale
hotspots.text: An isometric camera close to the roofs keeps the game cosy instead of map-like.

projects.title: Voicer
projects.oneLiner: Hold Fn and talk: local Whisper types your speech into any window.

hotspots.title: Hold Fn. Speak. Release.
hotspots.text: The whole product is one gesture, so it fits into any app without a new habit.

hotspots.title: Text lands at the cursor
hotspots.text: Dictation goes into whatever field is focused: notes, mail, code.

hotspots.title: Quiet recording pill
hotspots.text: A small pill with a waveform shows it is listening, then gets out of the way.

projects.title: Blackout
projects.oneLiner: Crack a safe in a dark room with friends; each phone holds a different tool.

hotspots.title: Join by QR
hotspots.text: Phones join by scanning the code on the TV: no app, no accounts.

hotspots.title: Different tool on every phone
hotspots.text: Each player gets a different tool (flashlight, scanner, terminal), so nobody can solve it alone.

hotspots.title: Start when ready
hotspots.text: The host starts when everyone is in; the button stays disabled until then.

projects.title: AURORA
projects.oneLiner: Descend into a powerless complex with friends to recover 2 fuel cells.

hotspots.title: QR plus room code
hotspots.text: Scan, or type the four-letter code: both paths are on screen for any phone.

hotspots.title: Mission in one sentence
hotspots.text: The brief fits in two lines under the title, read aloud by whoever holds the remote.

hotspots.title: One start button
hotspots.text: A single button keeps the lobby calm for a group of people looking at one TV.

projects.title: Quirky
projects.oneLiner: Capture text, colors, DOM elements, SVGs and pixel measurements on screen.

hotspots.title: Mode switcher
hotspots.text: Hex, OCR, DOM, SVG and pixel measuring live in one row, so switching tools costs one click.

hotspots.title: Pick anything
hotspots.text: Click any pixel on screen: the colour or element is captured and copied.

hotspots.title: Copy-ready output
hotspots.text: The result is shown in the format you will paste, not as raw data.

projects.title: Timex site
projects.oneLiner: Landing page for Timex, a terminal-style time tracker.

hotspots.title: Benefit, not features
hotspots.text: 'Type. The hour logs itself.' explains the product in five words.

hotspots.title: Download first
hotspots.text: The primary button goes straight to the signed Mac download.

hotspots.title: Sticky download
hotspots.text: The download button stays in the header while scrolling.

projects.title: Bunker Defense
projects.oneLiner: Be the drone: sweep your beam over monsters, build walls, survive 6 waves.

hotspots.title: Defend the core
hotspots.text: The core sits in the middle and everything moves toward it, so the threat is always readable.

hotspots.title: Wave timer
hotspots.text: Time to the next wave is in the corner of the big screen, like a scoreboard.

hotspots.title: Hint at the bottom
hotspots.text: One line of help explains the next action without pausing the game.

projects.title: Timex
projects.oneLiner: Keyboard-driven time tracker in a terminal UI, with client-ready reports.

hotspots.title: Timer that is always on
hotspots.text: The running task and its time are on top, the first thing you see.

hotspots.title: Type to start
hotspots.text: Type what you are working on and press Enter: no forms, no mouse.

hotspots.title: Day timeline
hotspots.text: Entries stack into a timeline that becomes a client report at the end of the week.

projects.title: Nightrail
projects.oneLiner: Run a station: craft gear, grow the workshop tree and keep your crew going.

hotspots.title: Workshops first
hotspots.text: The craft tab opens on what you can build right now, with resources counted on top.

hotspots.title: Skill tree as cards
hotspots.text: Each workshop upgrade is a card with its bonus and cost, so choices compare side by side.

hotspots.title: Five tabs
hotspots.text: Station, Crafts, Map, Crew, Profile: the whole game is reachable with one thumb.

projects.title: Kerbside
projects.oneLiner: Mobile car diagnostics: a mechanic comes to your driveway.

hotspots.title: Where the service happens
hotspots.text: 'The garage comes to you' is both the headline and the product.

hotspots.title: Booking right in the hero
hotspots.text: Postcode, symptom and day: availability is checked without leaving the first screen.

hotspots.title: Proof in numbers
hotspots.text: Vehicles fixed, average time on site and rating, right under the booking form.

projects.title: Calista Law
projects.oneLiner: Concept site for a UK Global Talent visa service for designers.

hotspots.title: Speaks to designers
hotspots.text: The headline talks to the audience in their language: 'the strength of your work'.

hotspots.title: Free assessment
hotspots.text: A free first step lowers the barrier before a paid visa service.

hotspots.title: Numbers that matter
hotspots.text: Fees, years to settlement and the endorsing bodies are shown as plain facts.

projects.title: Paper Dragon
projects.oneLiner: Guide a paper dragon through a night lantern festival, dodging storms.

hotspots.title: Dragon made of lanterns
hotspots.text: The dragon's tail grows with every lantern collected, so the score is drawn on screen.

hotspots.title: One-line goal
hotspots.text: 'Collect lanterns, avoid the storm clouds': the rule fits in a single line.

hotspots.title: Score in the corner
hotspots.text: A big white number, no frame: it stays readable on the dark night sky.

projects.title: Planet Drop
projects.oneLiner: Drop planets into a glass jar and merge matching ones into bigger worlds.

hotspots.title: A jar as the board
hotspots.text: The glass jar is the playfield and the fail line at once: 'keep below this line'.

hotspots.title: Aim from the top
hotspots.text: The next planet hangs above the jar with arrows, so aiming needs no explanation.

hotspots.title: Next up
hotspots.text: The queue on the right lets players plan merges a step ahead.

projects.title: Corder landing
projects.oneLiner: Landing page for Corder, the Mac meeting recorder.

hotspots.title: Promise in three words
hotspots.text: 'Just Record Everything' sells the product before any feature list.

hotspots.title: Download is the main action
hotspots.text: One green button to the Mac download; GitHub stars as social proof next to it.

hotspots.title: The real app below
hotspots.text: The hero shows the actual interface, not an illustration, so visitors see what they get.

projects.title: Qeepl
projects.oneLiner: Infinite zoomable canvas for terminals, browsers, VS Code and notes.

projects.title: WeddingStaffs
projects.oneLiner: Wedding invitation websites with RSVP, countdown and music, sold on Etsy.

hotspots.title: Category in two words
hotspots.text: 'Wedding Websites' and a one-line explanation: designs, RSVP, music, edited on your phone.

hotspots.title: Designs as products
hotspots.text: Each design is a card with a photo and short description, like a shop shelf.

hotspots.title: Try before you buy
hotspots.text: 'Try the editor' sits next to 'Buy on Etsy', so couples can play first.

projects.title: Logics7
projects.oneLiner: Site for a studio that builds digital products and business systems.

hotspots.title: What, for whom
hotspots.text: Digital products and business systems 'built to operate': the promise is about running, not launching.

hotspots.title: One clear next step
hotspots.text: 'Start a conversation' is the main action; the presentation is a quieter alternative.

hotspots.title: A real person
hotspots.text: The CEO's photo and role turn an agency page into a conversation with someone.

projects.title: Pult
projects.oneLiner: Control your Mac from iPhone and Apple Watch: trackpad, media, screen.

hotspots.title: Trackpad area
hotspots.text: A big touch area turns the iPhone into a trackpad for the Mac.

hotspots.title: Capture the mouse
hotspots.text: One button gives full control over the cursor, with a hotkey to release it.

hotspots.title: Media keys
hotspots.text: Play, pause and skip are always in reach, for the most common couch use.

projects.title: Hole City
projects.oneLiner: A hole roams the city, swallowing everything smaller and growing.

hotspots.title: The hole is the hero
hotspots.text: A black hole in a bright town reads instantly; nothing else on screen is that dark.

hotspots.title: Next size goal
hotspots.text: The bar shows how much you have to swallow to grow to the next size of objects.

hotspots.title: Size in metres
hotspots.text: Showing the hole's size in metres makes growth tangible.

projects.title: Piggy Run
projects.oneLiner: Run for coins, then build your own theme park.

hotspots.title: Gates that do the maths
hotspots.text: x2 and +10 gates turn a simple runner into a quick choice every second: greed or safety.

hotspots.title: Coins first
hotspots.text: The coin counter sits where the eye starts, because coins feed the theme park you build between runs.

hotspots.title: Progress bar, not a timer
hotspots.text: A thin level bar shows how far the finish is without adding pressure.

projects.title: Snake Arena
projects.oneLiner: Grow on coins, cut down rival snakes and beat the boss.

hotspots.title: Upgrades before the fight
hotspots.text: Start level, speed and item power are bought between rounds, so failing still feels like progress.

hotspots.title: One loud button
hotspots.text: FIGHT! is the only saturated button on screen; everything else is calm and secondary.

hotspots.title: Rivals you can read
hotspots.text: Each rival snake has its own colour and a name tag, so you know whom to cut off.

projects.title: Antistress
projects.oneLiner: 67 aimless mini-games: slice, squish, pop and drum.

hotspots.title: One shelf of toys
hotspots.text: 67 mini-games live on one scrolling shelf, so there is no menu tree to learn before the first tap.

hotspots.title: Search on top
hotspots.text: With this many toys, search beats categories: type 'pop' and you are playing in a second.

hotspots.title: Tiles you can read
hotspots.text: Big rounded tiles with a single object each read at thumbnail size on a phone, which is where Playables are opened.

projects.title: Punch Time
projects.oneLiner: Tap the guy, the boxing glove on a stick fires and sends him flying.

hotspots.title: One instruction
hotspots.text: 'Tap To Hit!' is the whole tutorial: the game is understood before the hand reaches the screen.

hotspots.title: The glove is the button
hotspots.text: The glove on a stick points at the target, so players know what the tap will do.

hotspots.title: Ragdoll payoff
hotspots.text: The target flies in a different arc every time, which is what makes people tap again.

projects.title: Sky Roll
projects.oneLiner: Swipe to roll a ball along a sky track to the finish.

hotspots.title: Ball in the centre
hotspots.text: The camera keeps the ball centred so a swipe always means the same thing, whatever the curve ahead.

hotspots.title: Lives as stacked balls
hotspots.text: Remaining lives are shown as balls on the track itself, not as a number in a corner.

hotspots.title: Swipe hint where the thumb is
hotspots.text: The hint sits exactly where the thumb rests, then disappears after the first swipe.

projects.title: Way Home
projects.oneLiner: Draw each parent a path to the house of their colour.

hotspots.title: Goal at the top
hotspots.text: The house of the matching colour sits at the far end, so the path you draw always reads bottom to top.

hotspots.title: Start where the finger is
hotspots.text: The parent stands near the thumb: drawing starts without reaching across the screen.

hotspots.title: Instruction in four words
hotspots.text: 'Draw a path home' is the full rule set; level 1 teaches the rest.

projects.title: Ninja Sneak
projects.oneLiner: Sneak up on guards from behind and stay out of the light.

hotspots.title: Light cones
hotspots.text: Guards show their field of view as a soft cone, so stealth is readable without any HUD.

hotspots.title: Drag anywhere
hotspots.text: The control ring appears where you touch: no fixed joystick to look for.

hotspots.title: Guards counter
hotspots.text: 'Guards 0/1' tells you the level goal in the same place on every level.

projects.title: Shiny Wash
projects.oneLiner: Hose off the mud, foam, scrub and dry the car to a shine.

hotspots.title: Progress you can see
hotspots.text: The percentage bar fills as mud disappears, so the player knows when the stage is done.

hotspots.title: Tactile cursor
hotspots.text: The hand cursor and the spray match the real gesture, which makes the cleaning satisfying.

hotspots.title: Tool switch
hotspots.text: One round button swaps hose, foam and dryer at the bottom, in reach of the thumb.

projects.title: Snip Salon
projects.oneLiner: Comb, cut along the line, dye and blow-dry.

hotspots.title: Cut-line meter
hotspots.text: The meter at the top shows how close the cut is to the dotted line: a clear score without numbers.

hotspots.title: Scissors in reach
hotspots.text: Tools rest on the right edge, where a right thumb already is.

hotspots.title: A face that reacts
hotspots.text: The doll reacts to each step, which turns a chore into a small story.

projects.title: Template Design
projects.oneLiner: Landing page for a wealth management advisory.

hotspots.title: Serif for trust
hotspots.text: Large serif type gives a wealth advisory the calm tone of a private bank.

hotspots.title: Book a review
hotspots.text: The main action is a 30-minute review: a low-commitment first step.

hotspots.title: People, not charts
hotspots.text: A photo of a team meeting instead of stock graphs keeps it human.

projects.title: Emigral tools
projects.oneLiner: Free UK immigration tools: sponsor licence and reference letter builders.

hotspots.title: Free, no sign-up
hotspots.text: The subtitle removes the two usual objections before the tools are shown.

hotspots.title: Tool cards
hotspots.text: Each tool says exactly which letter it builds and for which visa.

hotspots.title: Trustpilot rating
hotspots.text: Social proof sits right under the navigation, before the content.

projects.title: Pet in The System
projects.oneLiner: A pixel pet that walks on your windows, sleeps and gets thrown around.

projects.title: WGrid
projects.oneLiner: Snap windows into clean grids from the menu bar, drag to rearrange.

projects.title: Mixo
projects.oneLiner: Per-app volume mixer in the menu bar.

projects.title: Testio
projects.oneLiner: SaaS for running usability tests on live URLs.
